description: An examination of how Tanzania relates and cooperates with other nations and international organisations, the principles guiding its foreign policy, and the benefits and challenges of international cooperation.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by international relations?

options.text: The way different ethnic groups within one country interact
The interactions and relationships between states and other actors across national borders
The trade carried out only within a single country
The relationship between a government and its citizens

mcq.explanation: International relations refers to the political, economic, social and cultural interactions between sovereign states and other international actors beyond national boundaries.

mcq.questionText: Cooperation between only two countries is known as:

options.text: Multilateral cooperation
Bilateral cooperation
Regional cooperation
Universal cooperation

mcq.explanation: Bilateral cooperation involves two countries, for example an agreement between Tanzania and China, while multilateral cooperation involves three or more countries.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a principle guiding Tanzania's foreign policy?

options.text: Interference in the internal affairs of other states
Respect for the sovereignty and equality of all nations
Permanent military alliances with super powers
Colonisation of weaker neighbours

mcq.explanation: Respect for sovereignty and the equality of all nations is a core principle of Tanzania's foreign policy, alongside non-interference, good neighbourliness and peaceful coexistence.

mcq.questionText: In which year was the East African Community (EAC) re-established after its earlier collapse in 1977?
mcq.explanation: The Treaty re-establishing the EAC was signed in 1999 and entered into force on 7 July 2000, reviving the Community among Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda.

mcq.questionText: Where are the headquarters of the East African Community located?

options.text: Nairobi, Kenya
Kampala, Uganda
Arusha, Tanzania
Kigali, Rwanda

mcq.explanation: The headquarters of the East African Community are located in Arusha, Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: The policy of not joining any of the rival military power blocs is called:

options.text: Non-alignment
Good neighbourliness
Peaceful coexistence
Self-reliance

mcq.explanation: Non-alignment is the policy of refusing to take permanent sides with rival power blocs; Tanzania is a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement.

mcq.questionText: Which organisation was Tanzania a member of before it transformed into the African Union in 2002?

options.text: The League of Nations
The Organisation of African Unity (OAU)
The Pan-African Congress
The Frontline States Alliance

mcq.explanation: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU), founded in 1963, was transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002, with Tanzania as a member of both.

mcq.questionText: An official representative of a country who is sent to live and work in another country is called a:

options.text: Civil servant
Diplomat or ambassador
Migrant worker
Tourist

mcq.explanation: A diplomat, headed by an ambassador or high commissioner, represents his or her country's interests in a foreign state through the embassy or high commission.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes foreign aid?

options.text: Money a country collects from its own taxpayers
Assistance in the form of money, goods or services given by one country or organisation to another
Profit earned by a country from its exports
Loans given by one citizen to another

mcq.explanation: Foreign aid is assistance such as grants, loans, technical help or goods given by one country or organisation to another, usually to support development or emergencies.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a disadvantage of depending heavily on foreign aid?

options.text: It can build new schools and hospitals
It can lead to loss of economic independence and acceptance of unfavourable conditions
It can bring new technology to the country
It can help during natural disasters

mcq.explanation: Heavy dependence on foreign aid can undermine economic independence and force a country to accept conditions (conditionalities) that may not serve its own interests.

mcq.questionText: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) was formed mainly to:

options.text: Create a single global currency
Promote regional economic development and integration in Southern Africa
Replace the United Nations in Africa
Form a military alliance against Europe

mcq.explanation: SADC aims to promote sustainable economic development, regional integration, peace and security among member states in Southern Africa, including Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Tanzania's strong support for liberation movements in Southern Africa is an example of which foreign policy principle?

options.text: Non-alignment only
Support for the liberation and self-determination of oppressed peoples
Interference for personal gain
Isolation from African affairs

mcq.explanation: Tanzania hosted liberation movements such as the ANC, FRELIMO and ZANU, reflecting its principle of supporting the liberation and self-determination of oppressed peoples.

mcq.questionText: The main organ of the United Nations responsible for maintaining international peace and security is the:

options.text: General Assembly
Security Council
Secretariat
International Court of Justice

mcq.explanation: The UN Security Council has the primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security, including authorising peacekeeping missions.

mcq.questionText: The Commonwealth is an association made up mainly of:

options.text: Former French colonies
Countries that were formerly part of the British Empire
Only Asian countries
Countries that share one common currency

mcq.explanation: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of independent states, most of which were formerly part of the British Empire, including Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a key benefit Tanzania gains from regional integration through the EAC?

options.text: Reduced trade and a smaller market
A larger common market and easier movement of goods, services and people
Complete loss of its national sovereignty
Withdrawal from all other organisations

mcq.explanation: Regional integration in the EAC creates a larger common market, easing the movement of goods, services, capital and people, which expands trade opportunities for Tanzania.

fib.questionText: Cooperation involving three or more countries is known as _____ cooperation.
fib.explanation: Multilateral cooperation involves three or more countries, such as membership in the United Nations or the African Union.

fib.questionText: The headquarters of the East African Community are located in the city of _____ in Tanzania.
fib.explanation: Arusha, in northern Tanzania, hosts the headquarters of the East African Community.

fib.questionText: The principle of not taking permanent sides with rival power blocs is called _____.
fib.explanation: Non-alignment guides Tanzania to remain independent of rival military and political blocs; it is a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement.

fib.questionText: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was transformed into the African Union in the year _____.
fib.explanation: The OAU, founded in 1963, was officially transformed into the African Union (AU) in 2002.

fib.questionText: An office that represents one country within another country and is headed by an ambassador is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An embassy (or high commission for Commonwealth countries) represents a sending state in a host country and is headed by an ambassador or high commissioner.

fib.questionText: The principle of maintaining friendly relations with countries that share a common border with Tanzania is called _____.
fib.explanation: Good neighbourliness guides Tanzania to keep peaceful and friendly relations with its bordering states such as Kenya, Uganda, Zambia and Mozambique.

fib.questionText: The United Nations was established in the year _____ after the Second World War.
fib.explanation: The United Nations was established in 1945 to promote international peace, security and cooperation after the Second World War.

fib.questionText: The art and practice of conducting negotiations between nations through official representatives is called _____.
fib.explanation: Diplomacy is the conduct of relations between states through negotiation by accredited representatives such as diplomats and ambassadors.

fib.questionText: Foreign aid given without the requirement of repayment is known as a _____.
fib.explanation: A grant is foreign aid given freely without an obligation to repay, unlike a loan which must be paid back, often with interest.

fib.questionText: Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda first formed the original East African Community in the year _____ before it collapsed in 1977.
fib.explanation: The original East African Community was formed in 1967 by Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda but collapsed in 1977; it was later revived in 2000.

tf.questionText: Bilateral cooperation involves only two countries.
tf.explanation: Bilateral cooperation is between two countries, while multilateral cooperation involves three or more.

tf.questionText: Non-interference means that Tanzania should freely interfere in the internal affairs of other states.
tf.explanation: Non-interference is exactly the opposite; it means respecting the right of other states to manage their own internal affairs.

tf.questionText: Tanzania is a member of the United Nations.
tf.explanation: Tanganyika joined the UN in 1961, and Tanzania remains an active member, including serving on the Security Council in the past.

tf.questionText: The headquarters of the African Union are located in Arusha, Tanzania.
tf.explanation: The headquarters of the African Union are in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia; Arusha hosts the East African Community.

tf.questionText: Foreign aid sometimes comes with conditions that the receiving country must accept.
tf.explanation: Aid often carries conditionalities, such as policy reforms or procurement requirements, which can reduce the recipient's independence.

tf.questionText: Tanzania hosted several liberation movements such as FRELIMO and the ANC during the struggle against colonialism and apartheid.
tf.explanation: As part of its support for liberation, Tanzania hosted movements including FRELIMO of Mozambique and the ANC of South Africa.

tf.questionText: Peaceful coexistence means solving international disputes through war rather than dialogue.
tf.explanation: Peaceful coexistence means living and cooperating with other nations peacefully and resolving disputes through dialogue and negotiation, not war.

tf.questionText: The Commonwealth is made up mainly of countries that were formerly part of the British Empire.
tf.explanation: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of mostly former British territories, including Tanzania.

tf.questionText: Regional integration in the East African Community helps to enlarge the market available to Tanzanian producers.
tf.explanation: Integration creates a common market, giving Tanzanian goods access to a larger regional market and boosting trade.

tf.questionText: An ambassador works at the embassy of his or her home country located in a foreign country.
tf.explanation: An ambassador heads the embassy of the sending country within the host nation and represents its interests there.

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning of international relations.
summary.correctAnswer: International relations means the political, economic, social and cultural interactions and relationships that take place between sovereign states and other international actors across national borders.
summary.explanation: It captures how countries deal with one another beyond their borders through diplomacy, trade and cooperation.

summary.questionText: Differentiate between bilateral and multilateral cooperation.
summary.correctAnswer: Bilateral cooperation is cooperation between only two countries, while multilateral cooperation is cooperation involving three or more countries or organisations.
summary.explanation: An example of bilateral cooperation is an agreement between Tanzania and China; an example of multilateral cooperation is the United Nations.

summary.questionText: State four principles that guide Tanzania's foreign policy.
summary.correctAnswer: Four principles are: respect for the sovereignty and equality of nations, non-interference in the internal affairs of other states, good neighbourliness, and peaceful coexistence (others include non-alignment and support for liberation).
summary.explanation: These principles, rooted in Tanzania's history, shape how it relates with other countries.

summary.questionText: Mention three benefits Tanzania gains from international cooperation.
summary.correctAnswer: Tanzania gains access to a larger market and trade, financial and technical assistance for development, transfer of technology and skills, and support in maintaining peace and security.
summary.explanation: Cooperation brings economic, social and political advantages that a single country could not achieve alone.

summary.questionText: Identify three challenges of international cooperation.
summary.correctAnswer: Challenges include unequal benefits favouring stronger nations, loss of some sovereignty in decision-making, harmful conditions attached to aid and trade, competition that can hurt local industries, and dependency on foreign assistance.
summary.explanation: While beneficial, cooperation also carries risks that can undermine weaker economies like Tanzania's.

summary.questionText: State the main aims of the United Nations.
summary.correctAnswer: The United Nations aims to maintain international peace and security, promote friendly relations among nations, foster international cooperation in solving economic, social and humanitarian problems, and promote respect for human rights.
summary.explanation: Established in 1945, the UN works to prevent war and promote global cooperation; Tanzania is a member.

summary.questionText: How does Tanzania benefit from being a member of the East African Community?
summary.correctAnswer: Tanzania benefits from a larger common market for its goods, free movement of people, goods, services and capital, joint infrastructure projects, employment opportunities, and stronger regional peace and security.
summary.explanation: EAC integration expands trade and cooperation among partner states, with the headquarters based in Arusha.

summary.questionText: Explain the advantages of foreign aid to a developing country like Tanzania.
summary.correctAnswer: Foreign aid can finance development projects such as roads, schools and hospitals, provide relief during disasters, bring new technology and skills, and supplement the national budget.
summary.explanation: When used wisely, aid supports development that domestic resources alone cannot cover.

summary.questionText: Explain the disadvantages or dangers of depending on foreign aid.
summary.correctAnswer: Dependence on foreign aid can lead to loss of economic independence, acceptance of unfavourable conditions, increased debt from loans, interference in internal affairs, and a culture of dependency that weakens self-reliance.
summary.explanation: Aid with conditions can compromise sovereignty and trap a country in debt and dependency.

summary.questionText: Explain the role of diplomacy and embassies in international relations.
summary.correctAnswer: Diplomacy is the practice of conducting relations between states through negotiation by official representatives, while embassies represent the sending country in a host country, protect its citizens, promote trade and cooperation, and gather information.
summary.explanation: Diplomats and embassies are the main channels through which countries maintain peaceful relations and pursue their interests abroad.

hoq.questionText: A powerful country offers Tanzania a large loan on condition that Tanzania must buy all project equipment from that country and follow its advice on national policy. Applying the principles of foreign policy, why should Tanzania be cautious about accepting such aid?

options.text: Because the loan is too small to be useful
Because such conditions can undermine Tanzania's sovereignty and economic independence, conflicting with the principle of non-interference
Because Tanzania is forbidden from receiving any foreign aid at all
Because accepting any loan automatically makes a country a colony

hoq.explanation: Tied aid with policy conditions can erode sovereignty and economic independence, conflicting with the principles of non-interference and self-reliance, so Tanzania must weigh such terms carefully.

hoq.questionText: Two neighbouring countries that both belong to the EAC and SADC have a border dispute. Based on Tanzania's foreign policy principles, what is the most appropriate way for the region to handle the conflict?

options.text: Encourage the stronger country to invade and seize the disputed land
Ignore the dispute since it is an internal matter for each country
Use peaceful negotiation and dialogue through regional bodies to resolve the dispute
Expel both countries from all regional organisations immediately

hoq.explanation: The principles of peaceful coexistence and good neighbourliness call for resolving disputes through dialogue and negotiation, often facilitated by regional bodies such as the EAC and SADC.

hoq.questionText: A student argues that Tanzania should leave all international organisations to become fully independent. Evaluating the costs and benefits, what is the strongest argument against this view?

options.text: Leaving would have no effect at all on Tanzania
Membership gives Tanzania access to larger markets, development assistance, technology and collective security that isolation would deny
International organisations pay all of Tanzania's national budget
Tanzania is legally banned from ever leaving any organisation

hoq.explanation: While membership has challenges, it provides major benefits such as expanded trade, aid, technology transfer and collective security; isolation would deny Tanzania these advantages and weaken its development and influence.
